fi-hemichromis-bimaculatus.title: Jewel Cichlid
fi-hemichromis-bimaculatus.summary: The jewel cichlid, Hemichromis bimaculatus, is a cichlid from Africa's western coast, between southern Guinea and central Liberia. Regularly seen in the trade and often sold as a community fish, it…
rows: Pairs or small groups depending on setup
Will eat nearly anything offered, though live foods will help to enhance the colouration of the fish.
Widespread down Africa 's western coast from South Guinea to Central Liberia.
notes: Provide a roomy aquarium with as many hiding places as possible to help disperse aggresion and provide sanctuary.
This can be achieved through the use of clay flower pots, rockwork arranged to form caves, driftwood and areas of dense planting.

fi-pelvicachromis-pulcher.title: Pelvicachromis pulcher
fi-pelvicachromis-pulcher.summary: The kribensis, Pelvicachromis pulcher, is a cichlid from Nigeria and Cameroon, found in still and slow-moving, heavily vegetated waters. One of the most common cichlids in the hobby since the 1950s,…
rows: Pairs or small groups depending on setup
notes: The tank should contain plenty of hiding places and potential spawning sites.
Clay pots and caves, roots and pieces of driftwood can all be used.

fi-etroplus-maculatus.title: Red Chromide Cichlid
fi-etroplus-maculatus.summary: The orange chromide, Pseudetroplus maculatus, is a euryhaline cichlid native to peninsular India and Sri Lanka. It mostly inhabits brackish estuaries, coastal lagoons and the lower reaches of rivers,…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
group of 8+ individuals should therefore be the minimum purchase and these will form a noticeable dominance hierarchy once sexual maturity is reached.

Herbivore / algae browser. Observations of wild fish suggest it to be something of a generalist with a tendency to graze aufwuchs and filamentous algae from solid surfaces although it has been observed acting as a 'cleaner' for the congener E.
Native to peninsular India and Sri Lanka.
notes: This species can be maintained in fresh or brackish water so long as acidic conditions are avoided.

Décor is largely down to personal choice although a degree of structure, perhaps incorporating a sandy substrate, variably-shaped rocks and some driftwood branches, would adequately simulate natural conditions.

fi-hemichromis-lifalili.title: Red Lifalili Jewel Cichlid
fi-hemichromis-lifalili.summary: The blood-red jewel cichlid, Hemichromis lifalili, is a cichlid endemic to the Democratic Republic of Congo. Often confused with H. bimaculatus, it has two black spots on the flanks against that…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Primarily carnivorous, but will accept virtually anything offered.
Endemic to the Democratic Republic of Congo.
notes: Provide a roomy aquarium with as many hiding places as possible to help disperse aggresion and provide sanctuary.
This can be achieved through the use of clay flower pots, rockwork (arrange this to form caves), driftwood and areas of dense planting.

fi-steatocranus-casuarius.title: Buffalo Head Cichlid
fi-steatocranus-casuarius.summary: The blockhead cichlid, Steatocranus casuarius, is a rheophilic cichlid from the Lower Congo River and its tributaries, Democratic Republic of Congo. Its swimbladder is modified to reduce buoyancy,…
rows: Pairs or small groups depending on setup
Omnivore. It will accept dried pellets or flakes, but these should be supplemented with regular feedings of live and frozen foods such as bloodworm and brineshrimp.
notes: A substrate of sand is best as the fish like to dig, often creating a network of caves and tunnels under the tank decor.

Furnish the aquarium with piles of rocks arranged to form caves, but ensure these are secure (we advise placing them on the aquarium base or using silicone to glue them together), so they are not likely to fall on burrowing fish!.

fi-pelmatochromis-thomasi.title: Dwarf Pelmatochromis Thomasi Cichlid
fi-pelmatochromis-thomasi.summary: Dwarf Pelmatochromis Thomasi Cichlid (Pelmatochromis thomasi) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 5.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-pundamilia-nyererei.title: Pundamilla Nyererei Cichlid
fi-pundamilia-nyererei.summary: Pundamilia nyererei is a maternally mouthbrooding cichlid endemic to Lake Victoria, recorded only from the southern part of the lake in Tanzania. It is mostly restricted to rocky, littoral habitats…
rows: Omnivorous by nature, with wild fish feeding chiefly on aquatic invertebrates and zooplankton.
Endemic to Lake Victoria which has a shoreline divided between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, although P.
notes: This species does not require a lot of open swimming space and displays a preference for rocky environments so much of the available space can be filled with rockwork arranged in such a way that many broken lines-of-sight are created.

fi-haplochromis-obliquidens.title: Haplochromis Obliquidens Cichlid
rows: Up to about 8.9 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-haplochromis-sauvagei.title: Rock Kribensis Cichlid
fi-haplochromis-sauvagei.summary: Haplochromis sauvagei is a species of cichlid endemic to Lake Victoria. This species reaches a length of 10.5 centimetres (4.1 in) SL. [ 2 ] Its specific name honours the French paleontologist and…
rows: Up to about 10.5 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-heterotilapia-buettikoferi.title: Heterotilapia Buttikofferi Cichlid
fi-heterotilapia-buettikoferi.summary: Heterotilapia Buttikofferi Cichlid (Heterotilapia buettikoferi) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 30.8 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-hemichromis-exsul.title: Turkana Jewel Cichlid
fi-hemichromis-exsul.summary: A jewel cichlid from Kenya's Lake Turkana, a hard, alkaline desert lake. One of the milder jewels, but still very territorial when it breeds.
rows: Males to about 4 in (10 cm), females about 3 in (7.5 cm)
36 in (90 cm) long or larger for a pair
Milder than most jewels, but highly territorial when spawning
A pair, or with robust fish suited to hard water
Omnivore; captive-bred fish take most foods. Feed a varied diet
notes: Rock work (lava rock suits it) with a little wood; it does not need plants.
Settled pairs breed often; the warmer end of the range encourages spawning.

sources.name: Practical Fishkeeping – The stunning cichlid of Lake Turkana

fi-paratilapia-polleni.title: Paratilapia polleni (Black Diamond Cichlid)
fi-paratilapia-polleni.summary: A large cichlid from Madagascar, jet black with shimmering gold-to-blue spots in adults. It is endangered in the wild; large- and small-spotted forms exist and shouldn't be mixed because they interbreed.
rows: Males about 11 in (28 cm); females usually about half that
48 × 18 in footprint (about 54 gal) as a minimum; much larger with other cichlids
Fairly peaceful with other species that are too big to eat, but aggressive to its own kind and very territorial when breeding; small fish will be eaten
Keep singly or as a pair unless the tank is very large
Predator by nature, but takes dead foods readily: carnivore pellets plus frozen and live foods. No mammal meat
Endemic to Madagascar, where it is widespread
notes: Give lots of hiding places (clay pots, roots, driftwood) over sand or fine gravel; plants are optional cover.

fi-blood-parrot-hybrid.title: Blood Parrot Cichlid (hybrid)
fi-blood-parrot-hybrid.sci: Hybrid cichlid (parentage uncertain; usually given as Amphilophus × Vieja or Heros)
fi-blood-parrot-hybrid.summary: A man-made hybrid cichlid first bred in Taiwan, with a round body and a small beak-like mouth that cannot fully close. Hardy and bold, it grows to about 8 in and needs foods small enough to scoop up.
rows: About 8 in (20 cm); "King Kong" lines grow larger
About 30 gallons for one at the very least; 55 gallons is the usual recommendation for an adult, plus about 20 gallons for each extra fish
Semi-aggressive and territorial, especially when spawning, but its small mouth makes it less able to hurt tankmates; it will eat small fish that fit
Keep one, or three or more; a pair often ends with one bullying the other
Small pellets it can swallow whole (floating pellets are easiest for it to scoop)
Man-made hybrid (first bred in Taiwan around 1986); not a wild species
notes: Strong filtration and regular gravel cleaning help, because it makes a lot of waste.
Black patches on young fish are common and usually fade with age; they can also signal stress.
Avoid fish that have been dyed or injected with color; dyeing can shorten their lives.

fi-flowerhorn-hybrid.title: Flowerhorn Cichlid (hybrid)
fi-flowerhorn-hybrid.summary: A man-made hybrid cichlid that first went on sale in Malaysia in the late 1990s, prized for bright colors and the big hump on the male's head. It is large, very territorial and usually kept alone, but becomes a very interactive pet.
rows: Males up to about 12 in (30 cm); females smaller. Short-bodied "bonsai" types stay near 6 in
About 70 gallons for one (at least 4 ft long and 2 ft wide); about 150 gallons for a pair
Highly territorial and aggressive; not for community tanks with smaller fish
Eats almost anything: cichlid pellets plus meaty live or frozen foods such as bloodworms, earthworms and crickets; vary the diet
Man-made hybrid (from red devil, trimac and blood parrot crosses); not a wild species
notes: Prone to hole-in-the-head disease and ich if water quality slips; keep up water changes.
Never release one: dumped flowerhorns have become invasive pests in parts of Asia.

fi-xystichromis-kyoga-flameback.title: Kyoga Flameback
fi-xystichromis-kyoga-flameback.summary: A colorful Victorian cichlid from the Lake Kyoga basin; males show yellow, lime green and red. Mildly aggressive, endangered in the wild, and a maternal mouthbrooder.
rows: 40 gal or larger for a small colony
Mildly aggressive; not a community fish
Omnivore: spirulina flakes, frozen foods and African cichlid pellets, plus greens
Uganda: Lake Nawampassa, Kyoga basin (Victorian Nile)
notes: Use sand or fine gravel with stacked rock caves; keep with other less aggressive cichlids, not mbuna.
Females hold eggs in their mouth for about two weeks.
